summary: Trojanized @7nohe/openapi-react-query-codegen executes obfuscated payload at install time via binding.gyp Python escape
details: The package ships a binding.gyp whose GYP `conditions` expression uses Python object-graph traversal (`().__class__.__base__.__subclasses__()` reaching `catch_warnings`._module.__builtins__) to invoke `__import__('os').system('node 3FWCvzduYZg.js')`. All identifiers and the command string are hidden as `\U000000xx` unicode escapes. Because npm auto-runs node-gyp on any package containing binding.gyp, this evaluates during `npm install` on every installer, without any declared lifecycle script. The referenced native source `dog.c` is not shipped, so no genuine native build occurs — the binding.gyp exists solely to execute the bundled JS. The invoked file 3FWCvzduYZg.js contains a ~1.6MB charcode array XOR-decoded with key 77 and passed to `Function(...)()`, wrapped in a try/catch that emits a benign `load:` log. The decoded body references numerous short suspicious domains (u.tt, t.uz, zy.yt, xyzu.uz, uy.xyz). The multi-megabyte encoded runtime blob and Python-sandbox-escape build file have no relationship to the package's advertised OpenAPI React Query codegen purpose, consistent with a trojanized copy of the legitimate package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
